_note: Shared worked-example inputs for FMS engineering item 6 (communication): guide docs/FMS system design/66_communication.md, tools/fmse/*.py, web/fmse6x*.js. All values are EXAMPLES. Everything here is deterministic: guide, tools and web must give IDENTICAL results (including the handshake log line by line). The 4 basic calculators of web/fmse6.js (CALC pn, ec, mb, hi) keep their formulas exactly - repeated below.

_formulas.pn_load: frame = max(64, io + 10 + 22) ; wire = frame + 20 ; bps = dev*wire*8/(cyc_ms/1000) ; load = bps/(spd_Mbit*1e6) ; verdict OK if load < 0.5
_formulas.ec_cycle: bytes = max(84, 14 + 2 + 12 + dev*bytes_per_slave + 4 + 20) ; t_wire_us = bytes*8/spd_Mbit ; t_us = t_wire_us + dev*fwd_us ; cycle_min_us = 1.25*t_us ; verdict <250 motion at 250 us, <1000 1 ms possible, else split
_formulas.mb_poll: req = ceil(regs/125) ; tr = rtt + resp [ms] ; cycle = ceil(dev/max(1,conn))*req*tr [ms] ; updates/s = 1000/cycle ; request 12 bytes, response 9 + 2*min(regs,125) bytes ; verdict <=100 handshakes ok, <=500 monitoring
_formulas.hist_volume: vps = tags*rate ; net_kbit = vps*bytes*8/1000 ; GB_day = vps*bytes*86400*comp/1e9 ; total = GB_day*days ; verdict < 500 GB fits
_formulas.latency: t_tx = wire_bytes*8/R ; base latency = (hops+1)*t_tx + hops*t_sw + length_m*5e-9 s (5 ns/m in copper or fibre) ; worst case with ONE maximum frame (max_wire_bytes) already being sent at each egress port = base + hops*max_wire_bytes*8/R (priority does not pre-empt a frame in transmission; IRT / TSN time slots remove this term). Report in microseconds.
_formulas.iolink: approximate M-sequence time: master_bytes = 2 + pd_out ; device_bytes = od + pd_in + 1 ; bits = 11*(master_bytes + device_bytes) + 10 ; t_msg = bits/baud ; cycle = max(t_msg, device_min_cycle) ; for each COM rate (COM1 4800, COM2 38400, COM3 230400 bit/s)
_formulas.opcua_load: notifications/s = items/(sampling_ms/1000)*change_ratio ; publish messages/s = subscriptions/(publishing_ms/1000) ; bytes/s = notifications/s*bytes_per_notification + messages/s*overhead_per_message ; kbit/s = bytes/s*8/1000
_formulas.mqtt_load: msg_bytes = 2 + (len(topic) + 2) + metrics_per_msg*bytes_per_metric + sparkplug_header ; in msgs/s = edges*rate ; in B/s = in msgs/s*msg_bytes ; out B/s = in B/s*subscribers ; total kbit/s = (in + out)*8/1000
_formulas.fibre: loss = length_km*att_db_km + connectors*conn_db + splices*splice_db ; budget = tx_min_dbm - rx_sens_dbm ; margin = budget - loss ; OK if margin >= 3 dB
_formulas.subnet: CIDR a.b.c.d/p: mask = p ones ; network = ip AND mask ; broadcast = network OR NOT mask ; usable hosts = 2^(32-p) - 2 (p <= 30) ; first = network+1, last = broadcast-1 ; overlap of two subnets = one network contains the other's network address
_formulas.ip_plan: exactly as web/fmse6.js drawIP: third octet = vlan % 256 ; subnet 10.site.third.0/24 ; gateway .1 ; counters per module code give unit = UNIT code + 2-digit number ; for each device of MODDEV[module] (in order) take the next free address of its range group (RANGES start .10/.50/.100/.150/.200/.240) ; tag = cell.unit ; if beyond the range end -> 'range full!'
_formulas.profinet_name: PROFINET device name = lower-case '<cell>-<unit>-<slug>' where slug = device name in lower case, every run of characters outside a-z0-9 replaced by one '-', leading/trailing '-' removed ; rules: only a-z 0-9 '-' '.', each label <= 63, total <= 240, not starting with 'port-' ; e.g. FMS1 MC01 'PLC (machine)' -> fms1-mc01-plc-machine
_formulas.modbus_encode: INT -> one register two's complement 16 bit ; UINT/WORD -> one register ; DINT -> two registers HIGH WORD FIRST (this standard, 'ABCD') ; REAL -> IEEE 754 single, two registers high word first ; register bytes big-endian. Word-order variants for teaching: ABCD (standard), CDAB (word swap), BADC (byte swap), DCBA (both).
_formulas.modbus_frames: MBAP = transaction id (2) + protocol id 0 (2) + length (2) = bytes that follow (unit id + PDU) + unit id (1). FC03 request PDU = 03 start(2) qty(2) ; response = 03 bytecount(1) data. FC06 request/response = 06 addr(2) value(2). FC16 request = 10 start(2) qty(2) bytecount(1) data ; response = 10 start(2) qty(2). Exception response = (fc + 0x80) code. Codes: 01 illegal function, 02 illegal data address, 03 illegal data value (e.g. qty 0 or > 125 for FC03, > 123 for FC16), 04 server device failure. Order of checks in the example server: function supported -> quantity valid (03) -> address range inside the map (02) -> write allowed (only words with direction in or in/out, else 02). Frames written as upper-case hex bytes separated by one space.
_formulas.risk: risk = likelihood (1-5) * consequence (1-5) ; class high >= 15, medium 8-14, low <= 7 ; SL-T from the initial class: high 3, medium 2, low 1 ; residual likelihood = max(1, L - sum of countermeasure points) ; residual risk = residual L * C (same classes) ; zone SL-T = max SL-T of the threats of the zone
_formulas.firewall: rules are checked top-down, FIRST MATCH wins ; a rule field matches if equal or '*' ; no match -> default deny (rule id 'DEFAULT') ; flows inside one zone are not filtered (not tested here). Audit: an ALLOW rule whose zones are not neighbours (list 'neighbours', either direction) -> finding 'crosses zones' ; an ALLOW rule with service '*' -> finding 'any service'.

_rules: Discrete ticks k = 0,1,...,K; one tick = 100 ms = the poll period of the cell controller (CC). Two actors: CC and the module (MOD). CC image (written only by CC): Request, Ack, JobId, HB (heartbeat counter). MOD image (written only by MOD): Ready, Busy, Done, HSReady, HB, JobId. Initial: CC image all 0; MOD image Ready=1, others 0; MOD state IDLE; CC state S0; watch timers last=0, seen=0.

ONE-TICK DELAY: at the start of tick k take snapshots snc (CC image) and snm (MOD image) = values at the end of tick k-1. Both actors decide ONLY on the snapshot of the other side and write their own image (visible to the other side at tick k+1). Order inside a tick (also the log order): 1 events, 2 MOD, 3 CC.

1 EVENTS with time k in list order: MOD_FREEZE (module PLC stops: MOD does nothing at all, its image and HB stay frozen; remember freeze start f); MOD_RESUME (MOD runs again; set MOD watch timer last=k and seen=snc.HB; if MOD state EXEC: end = end + (k - f)); CC_FREEZE / CC_RESUME (same for CC: on resume CC sets last=k, seen=snm.HB and continues in its stored state); IGNORE_REQ_ON / IGNORE_REQ_OFF (module fault: MOD does not accept a request while ON); CC_RESET (operator reset: if CC state is ERR -> state S0, state timer = k). Log 'k EVENT <kind>'.

2 MOD (skip if frozen): (a) heartbeat: if k>0 and k % hb_period_ticks == 0 -> MOD.HB += 1. (b) watch CC heartbeat: if snc.HB != seen -> seen = snc.HB, last = k. If not lost and k - last >= hb_timeout_ticks -> lost, log 'MOD CC_LOSS', if state IDLE set Ready=0. Else if lost and last == k -> not lost, log 'MOD CC_OK', if state IDLE set Ready=1. (c) state machine, at most ONE transition per tick, checked in this order: IDLE and not lost and not ignoring and snc.Request==1 -> JobId=snc.JobId, HSReady=1, Busy=1, Ready=0, state ACCEPT, log 'MOD ACCEPT <job>'. ACCEPT and snc.Request==0 -> HSReady=0, end = k + exec_ticks, state EXEC, log 'MOD START <job>'. EXEC and k >= end -> Busy=0, Done=1, state DONE, log 'MOD DONE <job>'. DONE and snc.Ack==1 -> Done=0, Ready = 0 if lost else 1, state IDLE, log 'MOD RELEASE <job>'.

3 CC (skip if frozen): (a) heartbeat: if k>0 and k % hb_period_ticks == 0 -> CC.HB += 1. (b) watch MOD heartbeat: if snm.HB != seen -> seen = snm.HB, last = k. If not lost and k - last >= hb_timeout_ticks -> lost, Request=0, Ack=0, if state != ERR then state OFFLINE (timer k), log 'CC COMM_LOSS'; nothing else this tick. Else if lost and last == k -> not lost, log 'CC COMM_OK', then if state OFFLINE do RESYNC: snm.Done==1 -> Ack=1, state S4, log 'CC RESYNC_DONE <job>'; else snm.Busy==1 -> state S3, log 'CC RESYNC_BUSY <job>'; else state S0, log 'CC RESYNC_IDLE' and the current job (if any) goes back to the FRONT of the job queue; nothing else this tick. While lost: nothing else.

(c) CC state machine (state timer t = tick of the last state change; success condition is checked BEFORE the timeout): S0 WAIT_READY: if jobs remain and snm.Ready==1 and snm.Busy==0 -> take the first job, JobId=job, Request=1, state S1, log 'CC REQUEST <job>'. S1 WAIT_ACCEPT: snm.HSReady==1 -> Request=0, state S2, log 'CC ACCEPTED <job>'; else if k - t >= hs_timeout_ticks -> Request=0, state ERR, the job goes back to the FRONT of the queue, log 'CC HS_TIMEOUT S1 <job>'. S2 WAIT_RELEASE: snm.HSReady==0 -> state S3, log 'CC RUNNING <job>'; else timeout -> ERR, log 'CC HS_TIMEOUT S2 <job>'. S3 WAIT_DONE: snm.Done==1 -> Ack=1, state S4, log 'CC DONE <job>'; else if k - t >= job_timeout_ticks -> ERR, log 'CC JOB_TIMEOUT <job>'. S4 WAIT_DONE_CLEAR: snm.Done==0 -> Ack=0, state S0, job completed at tick k, log 'CC COMPLETE <job>'; else timeout -> Ack=0, ERR, log 'CC HS_TIMEOUT S4 <job>'. ERR: nothing (waits for CC_RESET).

KPIs per scenario: log lines, completed jobs with completion tick, final CC state, number of HS/JOB timeouts, comm-loss detection delay = tick of 'CC COMM_LOSS' (or 'MOD CC_LOSS') minus the freeze tick. Log line format: '<k> <text>' with k integer ticks.
